title: FirstPulse API credits & hosting fit - discovery
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private fit
summary: Discovery call with FirstPulse Health exploring Redwood API quickstart credits and which hosting mode fits their HIPAA-sensitive workflows. Customer is interested in a short pilot (2-4 weeks) to validate latency and PII handling; procurement timeline longer. SE requested sample prompt set for bench runs, AE to share security pack and pricing options.
action_items: Maya: send Redwood security packet (SOC2 audit, HIPAA note, KMS integration) by 2027-06-01
Liam: propose benchmark run plan + required sample data format by 2027-06-02
Priya: share sample prompt set and expected QPS profile by 2027-06-04
next_steps: Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) to run benchmarks against their prompt set
Enable trial account with free credits and instructions for time-to-first-token quickstart
Provide pricing options for Hosted, Dedicated reserved pool (monthly), and Private VPC license
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-30 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dr Aaron, Sofia, Priya (FirstPulse)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. i'm maya from redwood inference, ae on the account. um, real quick intros?
[00:05] Dr. Aaron: hi all, aaron here, head of data at FirstPulse. i'm joined by sofia and priya.
[00:09] Sofia: hey, sofia platform eng, working on infra for our new clinical summarization product.
[00:12] Priya: priya, cto, i'll chime on integration and procurement questions.
[00:16] Maya: awesome, quick agenda — understand your use case + constraints, talk hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private), discuss credits/quickstart and time-to-first-token, and define next steps. sound good?
[00:23] Priya: yep, sounds good.
[00:25] Liam: hi all, liam, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll jump into latency and benchmarks later.

Summary (auto): customer building clinical note summarization and triage assistant. primary concerns are PHI/HIPAA compliance, latency under 600ms P95 for short summaries, and predictable cost. interested in trying hosted API with credits but may move to dedicated or private depending on audit and residency needs.

[02:05] Dr. Aaron: to give some context — we ingest EHR notes and want quick summaries and some redaction. the models will see PHI, so data handling is a blocker. current proto uses an open-source model hosted in-house but it's expensive to operate and slow.
[02:28] Maya: got it. when you say slow, ballpark p95?
[02:31] Dr. Aaron: around 1.2 to 1.8 seconds for a 250-token output on our infra, plus we have multi-tenant overhead.
[02:38] Liam: okay, so latency target?
[02:40] Priya: for triage and clinician view we want under 600ms p95, ideally 300 to 400ms for small prompts.

[03:00] Maya: cool — that's a good target. quick question on deployment preference: are you leaning self-serve hosted to start, or do you already require a dedicated or private deployment because of compliance?
[03:12] Priya: we'd like to test hosted first if the data handling guarantees are sufficient. procurement is slow though — even for a pilot we need to confirm SOC2 + HIPAA, and KMS for key control.
[03:24] Maya: totally reasonable. our hosted API is commonly used for pilots; we offer a security pack that outlines SOC2, encryption at rest/in-transit, and options for customer-managed keys with our Dedicated/Private tiers. for hosted we can discuss a limited PHI handling agreement for pilot, or you can run a pseudonymized dataset.

[04:00] Dr. Aaron: is there a mechanism to keep logs or tokens out of retention? we need audit logs but not content retention for PHI.
[04:08] Liam: yes — we have configurable retention windows and enterprise customers can request zero-retention or more strict retention. with Dedicated/Private you get more control and you can route logs to your SIEM.
[04:20] Sofia: and how about kms — can we bring our own keys?
[04:24] Maya: for Private, yes BYOK with HSM integrations; for Dedicated you can use customer-managed KMS in many cases; hosted supports server-side encryption and we can discuss customer key options for enterprise plans. i'll include the specifics in the security packet.

[05:10] Priya: procurement timeframe — if we like the pilot, we'd likely move to negotiation for dedicated capacity in ~6-8 weeks, but the proof-of-concept itself we'd like 2-4 weeks to validate latency/quality.
[05:23] Maya: that matches a lot of other customers. for time-to-first-token — with our quickstart and free credits we typically see teams making first calls within a few hours: create an API key, run the sample curl or SDK, and we can even pre-seed a small bench on Redwood side.
[05:38] Dr. Aaron: a few hours? we have internal change control — might be a bit longer, but good to hear.

[06:00] Liam: quick architecture note — latency depends on model choice, sequence length, and batch settings. for 250-token outputs our runtime can serve ~400ms p95 on certain quantized Llama-family variants on dedicated GPUs; hosted performance varies by region and model. we recommended continuous KV cache for chatty flows.
[06:22] Sofia: hmm, we do both one-off summaries and short conversational follow-ups, so KV cache might help.

[07:00] Maya: on cost tradeoffs — hosted is easiest but can be pricier at scale; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost with reserved commits; Private is for regulatory/air-gapped scenarios and has platform fees. we can run a quick cost estimate if you share QPS and typical token lengths.

[08:20] Dr. Aaron: on the model side — do you host open models only or do you also support proprietary weights?
[08:27] Liam: we support a catalog of open and vetted models; customers can also bring custom weights into Dedicated/Private installs with some licensing checks. for hosted we host curated open models and model variants optimized for latency.

[09:10] Priya: curious about fallbacks — if the primary model experiences latency or queueing, do you have automatic fallbacks?
[09:18] Maya: yes — we have smart routing and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants or different regions, configurable by policy. this helps reliability during spikes.

[10:05] Sofia: can we run a test where you host a few sample prompts and we measure p95?
[10:10] Liam: absolutely. usual cadence is: you send sample prompt set and expected QPS; we spin up a bench and run against hosted first using free credits and then we can run on a dedicated instance to compare.

[11:00] Dr. Aaron: sample dataset — will include PHI-like content but de-identified. expectation: redaction quality + summary quality.
[11:10] Maya: perfect. please include expected traffic and any SLOs.

[12:00] Priya: security review — we'll need SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. can your hosted offering integrate with our IdP for the console?
[12:10] Liam: hosted supports SSO for the console via SAML/OIDC for enterprise customers; for API keys we do token management and RBAC at the token level. Dedicated and Private give even more fine-grained RBAC and can integrate with your LDAP/IdP directly.

[13:05] Dr. Aaron: about data residency — we serve in the US only for now, but might expand to EU for partnerships. is multi-region supported?
[13:15] Maya: yes, hosted supports region selection in many cases; Dedicated can be provisioned in selected regions; Private obviously stays within your network. we'll include region availability matrix.

[14:00] Sofia: can you explain the quickstart flow — what's the path from sign-up to first successful API call?
[14:06] Maya: sure — step one: create account and get free credits (we usually provision a trial credit bundle), step two: create an API key, step three: run sample curl/SDK with example prompt. we have quickstart guides, SDKs for python/node, and a debug console. with an SE touchpoint we can do a guided run and get your first call in under a couple hours.
[14:30] Dr. Aaron: what's in the trial credits? is it model-limited?
[14:34] Maya: trial credits are general-purpose but we sometimes restrict access to certain large-model variants depending on availability. we'll clarify precisely which models are included in the trial for your account.

[15:00] Liam: if your priority is latency, we often recommend starting with a smaller quantized model variant for the bench and then test higher-quality variants for quality/regression tradeoffs.

[16:05] Priya: ok on cost modeling — if we do a 2-4 week pilot using hosted credits, and then assume 2000 summaries/day at average 150 output tokens, what ballpark should we expect?
[16:17] Maya: rough sketch: hosted per-token pricing varies by model; for a quantized medium variant you might see lower per-token than large. i'll put together an estimate table for hosted vs dedicated (reserved) vs private (license + infra) based on your numbers.

[17:05] Dr. Aaron: also interested in eval tooling — how do you detect quality regressions and get alerts?
[17:12] Liam: Redwood Optimize has eval hooks — you supply prompt/ground-truth sets and we run continuous quality monitoring with regression alerts, plus rollback/rollout policies. for pilot, you can run manual evals.

[18:00] Sofia: for the bench, what format do you need the prompts in? jsonl?
[18:04] Liam: jsonl is easiest — prompt, expected output, any metadata. include sequence length, expected tokens. also include anonymization notes.

[19:00] Dr. Aaron: compliance — HIPAA specific question: do you sign BAA for hosted pilots?
[19:08] Maya: yes, we have a BAA process for enterprise customers; pilot BAA is possible but sometimes teams run de-identified data first while paperwork completes. we'll share our legal playbook for BAAs.

[20:10] Priya: procurement will push back on change to keys and data flows — what friction have you seen?
[20:16] Lily: (note: mis-attrib) i mean we've seen procurement want dedicated or private for PHI-heavy workloads; hosted pilots are accepted when there's clear isolation and short retention.
[20:30] Maya: (laugh) thanks — yes, predictable pattern.

[21:00] Liam: technical deep dive items: we'll want a sample prompt set, QPS profile, target latency SLOs, and any redaction rules. from that we can propose a bench matrix: hosted (region A) vs dedicated small pool vs dedicated medium pool and quantify latency/cost.

[22:00] Sofia: can you do a small demo of the sample curl? we can follow along.
[22:06] Maya: sure — i'll paste the minimal curl in the follow-up email, but quick verbal: curl header auth bearer api-key, post body with model, input, max_tokens, temperature. SDK shows same in python with client.generate().
[22:30] Sofia: ok that helps.

[24:00] Dr. Aaron: another question — are there guardrails for hallucination detection?
[24:06] Liam: we provide structured output support and you can use function/tool calling to constrain outputs; quality monitoring can catch steep regressions. we also have reranking and post-processing options.

[25:00] Priya: if we wanted to estimate dedicated sizing, what metrics do you need?
[25:06] Liam: typical inputs: avg tokens in + out, p95 latency target, expected concurrency / QPS during peak, and acceptable cost per 1k tokens. with that we map to GPU pool sizes and throughput.

[26:00] Maya: a few practical notes — we often provision a shadow dedicated instance for benchmarking if customers want a direct comparison. provisioning for dedicated can be done in days once terms are set.

[27:00] Sofia: can you confirm logs and auditability — we need request-level traces for debugging.
[27:08] Liam: yes, per-request tracing is available in the Redwood Console; you can export traces to tracing backends or keep them in our console. for privacy we can mask content fields in exported logs.

[28:20] Dr. Aaron: what does support look like during a pilot?
[28:25] Maya: AE + SE support for the pilot, weekly syncs, and a runbook for the bench. for enterprise pilots we often include faster ticket SLAs.

[29:30] Priya: let's talk red flags — things that would push us away from hosted to dedicated/private?
[29:36] Maya: biggest red flags are inability to meet data residency or BAA needs, need for complete zero-retention with customer keys, and significant throughput requiring cost predictability. any of those push to Dedicated or Private.

[31:00] Dr. Aaron: procurement will ask for references — can you share other healthcare customers?
[31:05] Maya: yes, we can share anonymized case studies and reference contacts after an NDA. i'll include the references pack.

[32:00] Sofia: regarding SDKs — do you have server-side batching and token accounting in the SDK?
[32:06] Liam: SDKs are client-side helpers; the runtime handles continuous batching and invoicing is token-accurate with logs that break down by route/model.

[33:20] Priya: for the pilot, our timeline is: legal signs BAA or we de-id data (1-2 weeks), tech bench (2 weeks), then procurement for dedicated (6-8 weeks).

[34:00] Maya: totally — sounds like a plan. i'll follow up with the security packet and a short guide to get first calls in.

[35:10] Dr. Aaron: quick nit — any constraints on sample size for the bench? we have about 500 example notes ready.
[35:18] Liam: 500 is more than enough; we usually do 100-200 for initial bench, then scale tests.

[36:05] Sofia: about regressions — can we pin model versions?
[36:10] Liam: yes, pinning versions and automatic rollback are supported so you don't get quality drift on an auto-updated model.

[37:00] Priya: ok, finance will want to see a committed monthly # for dedicated — do you have standard tiers?
[37:08] Maya: yes, standard reserved tiers for Dedicated with monthly commit levels; i'll include a tiered pricing sheet.

[38:30] Dr. Aaron: any gotchas we should know before doing the bench?
[38:36] Liam: small ones — ensure prompt formatting consistent, be explicit about stop tokens and max length, and provide an anonymized exemplar to test redaction. also watch for long context windows which affect throughput.

[39:45] Sofia: do you support on-prem packages?
[39:50] Maya: yes, our Private option is an on-prem offering with a customer-managed control plane; it's heavier lift but required for air-gapped environments. we'll include the on-prem checklist.

[41:00] Dr. Aaron: cool. any preliminary dates for the deep dive?
[41:06] Maya: how about we aim for next week for a 60-minute SE-led bench planning session?
[41:12] Priya: that works for us, mornings are better.

[42:00] Maya: recap — we'll: (1) send security packet + BAA process, (2) enable trial credits and quickstart guide, (3) Liam will outline benchmark plan, (4) Priya and Aaron will share sample prompts and QPS.

[43:15] Dr. Aaron: thanks everyone. excited to try it out.
[43:20] Priya: same — we'll aim to get prompts to you by Friday.
[43:25] Maya: perfect. i'll follow up with meeting notes and links.

[44:00] Sofia: one last thing — can you include an expected billing example for 2k summaries/day in the follow-up?
[44:05] Maya: yep, will include hosted vs dedicated cost table.

[45:00] Maya: ok wrapping — thanks for your time. we'll go offline on the next steps.
[45:10] Liam: thanks all.
[45:15] Dr. Aaron: bye.

(End of recording)
